title: Sheaf Hom applied to a finite presentation is a kernel of finite sums
statement:
Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space and $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules on (the open subsets of) $X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal F,\mathcal M$ let $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal M)$ be the sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom], with sections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal F|_U,\mathcal M|_U)$ over an open $U\subseteq X$, $\mathcal F|_U$ the restriction to $U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]; for $\psi$ such a section write $\psi_U:\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal M(U)$ for its component at $U$.

(1) Let $\mathcal E_2\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal E_1\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal E\to0$ be an exact sequence in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] and $\mathcal M$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module. Let $b^*:\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal E,\mathcal M)\to\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal E_1,\mathcal M)$ and $a^*:\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal E_1,\mathcal M)\to\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal E_2,\mathcal M)$ be precomposition, $b^*_U(\psi)=\psi\circ b|_U$, $a^*_U(\chi)=\chi\circ a|_U$. Then $b^*,a^*$ are morphisms of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal E,\mathcal M)\xrightarrow{b^*}\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal E_1,\mathcal M)\xrightarrow{a^*}\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal E_2,\mathcal M)$$
is exact in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$.

(2) For $n\ge0$ let $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}$ be the free $\mathcal O_X$-module with basis sections $e_1,\dots,e_n\in\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}(X)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], and for an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal M$ let $\mathcal M^{\oplus n}$ be the $\mathcal O_X$-module $U\mapsto\mathcal M(U)^{\oplus n}$ with componentwise restriction maps and $\mathcal O_X(U)$-action. Let $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus m}\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal H\to0$ be an exact sequence in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$, and let $a_{ik}\in\mathcal O_X(X)$ ($1\le i\le n$, $1\le k\le m$) be the coefficients with $a_X(e_k)=\sum_i a_{ik}e_i$. Then for every $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal M$ the sequence
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal H,\mathcal M)\xrightarrow{\beta}\mathcal M^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal M^{\oplus m},$$
$$\beta_U(\psi)=\bigl(\psi_U(b_U(e_i|_U))\bigr)_{1\le i\le n},\qquad \alpha_U\bigl((x_i)_{i}\bigr)=\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^n a_{ik}|_U\,x_i\Bigr)_{1\le k\le m}\quad(U\subseteq X\text{ open}),$$
consists of morphisms of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and is exact in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$.

proof.text: Step 1: Identify the source library homFunctor R, contravariant in its first variable, with the internal Hom of the symmetric monoidal closed structure on sheaves of modules. Components of the natural isomorphism are identities, and SheafOfModules.pre_app proves naturality. Mathlib CategoryTheory.ihom supplies preservation of limits by the contravariant internal Hom functor via the parametrized tensor-Hom adjunction. Thus homFunctor R flipped at M preserves equalizers and kernels.

proof.text: *Step 5 ($\mathcal Hom(\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n},\mathcal M)\cong\mathcal M^{\oplus n}$).* For an open $U$, $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}|_U$ is the free $\mathcal O_U$-module $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}$ with basis sections $e_i|_U$, and by [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] (on the ringed space $(U,\mathcal O_U)$) every $\mathcal O_U$-linear $\varphi:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal M|_U$ is the map $e_i|_U\mapsto s_i$ determined by sections $s_i\in\mathcal M(U)$, necessarily $s_i=\varphi_U(e_i|_U)$, and every tuple $(s_i)$ occurs. Hence $\theta^n_U:\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n},\mathcal M)(U)\to\mathcal M(U)^{\oplus n}$, $\varphi\mapsto(\varphi_U(e_i|_U))_i$, is bijective. It is additive and $\mathcal O_X(U)$-linear ($(f\varphi)_U(e_i|_U)=f\,\varphi_U(e_i|_U)$, Step 1), and compatible with restriction to $V\subseteq U$: $(\varphi|_V)_V(e_i|_V)=\varphi_V(e_i|_U|_V)=\varphi_U(e_i|_U)|_V$ by naturality of $\varphi$. So $\theta^n:\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n},\mathcal M)\to\mathcal M^{\oplus n}$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules (for $n=1$: $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X,\mathcal M)\cong\mathcal M$).

proof.text: *Step 6 (the maps in coordinates).* Since $a$ is a morphism of sheaves, $a_U(e_k|_U)=a_X(e_k)|_U=\sum_ia_{ik}|_U\,e_i|_U$. For $\varphi$ a section of $\mathcal Hom(\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n},\mathcal M)$ over $U$ with $\theta^n_U(\varphi)=(x_i)_i$, $\mathcal O_U(U)$-linearity of $\varphi_U$ gives $\theta^m_U(a^*_U\varphi)=\bigl((\varphi\circ a|_U)_U(e_k|_U)\bigr)_k=\bigl(\sum_ia_{ik}|_U\,x_i\bigr)_k=\alpha_U(\theta^n_U\varphi)$, so $\theta^m\circ a^*=\alpha\circ\theta^n$; and for $\psi$ a section of $\mathcal Hom(\mathcal H,\mathcal M)$ over $U$, $\theta^n_U(b^*_U\psi)=\bigl(\psi_U(b_U(e_i|_U))\bigr)_i=\beta_U(\psi)$, so $\theta^n\circ b^*=\beta$. In particular $\alpha=\theta^m a^*(\theta^n)^{-1}$ and $\beta=\theta^nb^*$ are morphisms of $\mathcal O_X$-modules (Steps 1, 5).
